$comment: Per-user Claude Code hooks — copy this file into place to register your own hooks,
which the shared settings.json will never overwrite.
Install:
cp global-settings/user-hooks.example.json ~/.claude/user-hooks.json
chmod 600 ~/.claude/user-hooks.json
# (optional) mirror the kernel lock the other hooks use:
sudo chattr +i ~/.claude/user-hooks.json
Schema:
Each top-level key is a Claude Code hook event. Each value is an array of
entries with two fields:
- command   Bash command line to run when the event fires. Stdin will be
the standard Claude Code hook JSON payload; stdout is
forwarded back to Claude (relevant for UserPromptSubmit,
which uses stdout as additional prompt context).
- matcher   (optional) Anchored ERE tested against tool_name for
PreToolUse / PostToolUse. Empty or omitted = fire on every
tool call. Ignored for events that carry no tool_name.
Exit codes:
- 0    normal completion.
- 2    hard-deny (only meaningful for PreToolUse). Propagated to Claude.
- any other non-zero code is logged to stderr and swallowed — a broken
personal hook must never wedge a Claude session.
The dispatcher (~/.claude/hooks/user-hooks-dispatch.sh) is registered once,
for every event, in the shared settings.json. You never touch settings.json;
you only touch this file. When the shared settings.json is bumped and
re-installed, this file is left completely alone.
Editing:
Claude is BLOCKED from modifying this file (see the deny list in the
shared settings.json and the two block-*-writes.sh hooks). Edit it in
your own terminal, exactly like ~/.claude/sound-config.sh.
The keys below are the complete set of Claude Code hook events. Leave any
you don't need as empty arrays — the dispatcher fast-paths past them.

$examples.$comment: Reference-only. Copy the entries you want into the arrays above; the dispatcher ignores anything under $examples.

UserPromptSubmit.$comment: Inject per-project plan context on every prompt (see ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/plans/hooks/plan-context.sh in the claude-plans-nc-server repo for the pattern).

PreToolUse.$comment: Fire only on Bash calls — a personal write-command guard on top of the shared one.
Fire on every tool call — an audit logger.
